map_order_whole_decimal_mixed.option: pool: whole numbers and decimals mixed (7, 6.85, 7.1, 0.9)
map_order_whole_decimal_mixed.name: Order Whole Numbers and Decimals Together
map_order_whole_decimal_mixed.teaches: Order a set that mixes whole numbers and decimals with different numbers of places
map_order_whole_decimal_mixed.representation: Print: one B&W boxed Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; the numbers in a row of boxes, pupil writes them in order in an empty box row under a least → greatest arrow. Screen: drag tiles into the ordered slots (production, never MC).
map_order_whole_decimal_mixed.why: MAP sets mix whole numbers and decimals; the trap (6.85 > 7 because it is longer) is never dealt today
problemTypes: Order 3 — three numbers, one whole (7) — write in order / drag tiles
Order 4–5 — mixed whole and 1-2 place decimals — write in order / drag tiles
Greatest or least — pick from a mixed set — ring it / click it
levels: L1: 3 numbers, a whole and decimals with the same whole part (7, 7.4, 6.9); place-value header over each number (structural, stays); 7 written as 7.0 in grey (hint)
L2: the 7.0 grey hint fades: 7 shown bare
L3: 4–5 numbers with different digit counts (0.9, 6.85, 7, 7.1)
L4: greatest → least direction

example.item: Write in order, least to greatest: 7.1, 6.85, 7, 0.9

misconceptions: A whole number has no tenths so it goes first or last
Longer number is bigger (6.85 > 7.1)

map_compare_pick.option: form: pick the greater / lesser (2–4 numbers; click one, or ring it on paper)
map_compare_pick.name: Which Is Greater? Which Is Less?
map_compare_pick.teaches: Choose the greatest or least of 2–4 whole numbers by comparing place by place
map_compare_pick.representation: Print: one B&W boxed Andika cell (WORKSHEET_DESIGN_STANDARD.md), big digits, single grey for structure only; 2–4 numbers each in its own box; pupil rings the greater (or lesser). Screen: click the number box (hot spot, a selection, not text MC).
map_compare_pick.why: MAP asks 'which number is greater' as a select item; we only deal the symbol
problemTypes: Pick the greater of two — two numbers — ring / click
Pick the least of 3–4 — a set — ring / click
Pick all greater than N — a set and a target — tick all / click all
levels: L1: two numbers to 10, tens frame under each (hint, fades)
L2: frames fade; numbers to 20
L3: 3–4 numbers to 100 with a place-value header (structural, stays)
L4: to 1,000; "choose all greater than"
misconceptions: Reads the first digit of the shorter number as larger (9 > 12)
Swaps "lesser" and "greater"

compare_sentences.why: MAP 'without calculating' items; compare_expressions only evaluates

compare story — more/fewer — build e.g. 14 − 6 = ☐ or 6 + ☐ = 14

L2: change unknown and start unknown (☐ moves)
L3: compare stories (bigger, smaller, difference unknown); underlining fades
L4: × ÷ stories, incl. unknown factor and sharing
L5: fraction stories (like denominators; fraction × whole)

Use the rule — one empty row — write the value

Applies the rule down the column (adds 6 each row) not across
